# api-next Very identity gate and community creation

## Guest participation successor, October 11, 2026

Website guest Study requires no account, persona, membership or Palm ceremony. Spec027 owns its narrow browser authority and prospective original-drawing participation. Joining a Palm-policy community still requires its Very proof; participant claim retains Spec015 section5.2a. This introduces no account-age assertion or adult-content capability.

See [Spec027](027-guest-study-original-drawing-participation.md). This is the
governed integration candidate; independent integration review and the frozen
API interface checkpoint remain required before delegated implementation.

## Account setup has no 16+ assertion, approved 2026-10-09

The workspace_owner explicitly removed the full-account 16+ requirement on
2026-10-09. Ordinary registration, existing-account sign-in and Telegram
account recovery or connection require no minimum-age self-attestation.
Remove the blanket authenticated-route attestation gate and the sign-in age
declaration. Neither registration nor repeated registration writes or fabricates
an age-attestation row. Existing assertions remain historical records; synthetic
fixture assertions never become evidence about a real learner.

Adult-resource access remains a separate content capability. The workspace_owner
made 18+ song handling low priority: use existing content checks where they are
already available, without adding an account-setup ceremony. Telegram practice
already lists general-rated songs only and retains that filter. This ruling
does not supply adult-resource proof or alter separate reward-eligibility rules.

## Telegram practice accounts carry no account-age assertion, 2026-10-08

The workspace_owner removed the in-chat 16-or-older action on 2026-10-08, after
testing the phase-one bot, and stated that they had not asked for it. This
supersedes the account-age path recorded here on 2026-10-06.

A restricted Telegram learner account is created on a deliberate lesson-start
action, which is the sender choosing a song from their own current list. No
account-age assertion is asked for or recorded. No minimum-age-attestation-v1
row is written for such an account, and none may be fabricated on the learner's
behalf. /study, a typed message or a navigation visit alone creates nothing.
Preserve the sender, bot, community and current ingress generation through
acceptance and retry deduplication.

Section 2.1 governs ordinary registration without an account-age assertion,
following the workspace_owner's 2026-10-09 ruling. A restricted practice account
carries no age assertion, including upon future account recovery or promotion.
This restricted practice path issues no browser session, records no birth date and
supplies no adult-resource, membership or reward eligibility evidence.
Affirmations recorded between 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-08 are kept as history.

## 1. Track

- Owning lanes: api-next identity lane (first serial charter on shared
  surfaces), then the Solid product-wiring tranche after its contracts exist.
- Start gate: acceptance of this spec. The M3 Self/funding ceremony and soak
  in spec 005 are a separate operational track, not an implementation gate for
  `very.web`, community creation, or the text happy path.
- Dependencies: gates-v2 decision record; the wizard lane's preserved branch
  `product/gate-wizard-stories@bd8cabf` (UI reference only; the lane is
  retired and the branch is story-owned and provider-neutral).
- Explicit exclusions: no per-action re-verification of existing members in v1;
  no `human.unique` emission; no `very.zk` provider; no evidence-minting mock
  mode; no legacy runtime import; no native OAuth authorization-code flow in
  this charter. The working legacy browser flow is the behavioral target:
  desktop uses the Very embedded widget and mobile uses the encrypted Very
  bridge/deep-link plus polling. The old browser fetch proxy, client-local
  trust, and verifier-5xx trust fallback remain excluded.

## 2. Claims and the curated human-membership policy

The first curated membership policy is:

`human.personhood + credential.subject_unique, same subject, at join`

- `credential.subject_unique` is derived only from the subject or pseudonym in
  the server-verified Very web session result and its persisted provider
  binding. It is never accepted from a browser payload.
- `human.personhood` carries `provider_attested` assurance from the completed
  palm-verification ceremony. It does not assert liveness and does not assert
  person-level deduplication.
- The evaluator slice extends `RequiredClaim` beyond the curated age trio and
  pins a new hash-anchored preimage (`curated-human-membership-v1`) following
  the exact canonical-preimage discipline of
  `packages/domain/src/gates-v2/evaluator.ts`. Any byte change requires a new
  revision and hash.
- `policy_version_id` identifies that canonical evaluator revision and is
  deliberately reusable by different communities. Its storage identity is
  `(community_id, policy_version_id)`, never a globally unique id and never a
  per-community rewrite of `curated-human-membership-v1`.
- Product copy may say "humans only". It must not promise Sybil resistance or
  one-person-one-account until Very documents person-level deduplication and a
  later policy revision earns `human.unique`.

A member policy is either the Palm policy or the document-nationality policy
(§2.2, 2026-09-19 amendment). The Palm policy contains `human-verification`
alone. The document-nationality policy contains `nationality-allowed` alone
and no `human-verification`. There is no empty or open member policy, and the
two policies are mutually exclusive. The product may describe the Palm policy
as materially reducing bots, spam, and duplicate-human abuse; it must not
claim that a verified or compromised account cannot automate activity.

### 2.1 Account age and adult-resource capability

Registration requires verified Privy proof through `POST /auth/register`, with
`privy_access_token` as its only required request field. The previously published
`minimum_age_attestation` field may remain optional and validated in the maintained
contract during the current-client rollout, but registration ignores it and
creates no assertion, including when a credential is already registered.
The website sends only the proof and makes no age declaration on the learner's
behalf. Preserve registration concurrency, candidate collision, credential
tombstone, account lifecycle, wallet preparation and browser-session boundaries.

An account without a historical 16+ assertion can use authenticated routes under
their ordinary authorization rules. Do not query the assertion table as a global
admission gate or return an age-attestation onboarding requirement. Existing
historical rows and an explicitly invoked historical assertion endpoint may be
retained; neither supplies adult-resource evidence nor imposes account setup.
This supersedes the 2026-08-26 account-age amendment above. No historic assertion
is fabricated, silently backfilled or deleted by this change.

The viewer capability for an `adult_18` resource is the curated account claim
`minimum_age: 18`, proved only through `self` or `zkpassport`. It reuses the
existing versioned curated minimum-age policy and is evaluated against the
private account, not a persona or community membership. Very personhood,
self-declaration, invitation, import, and operator action cannot satisfy it.
One accepted proof unlocks adult-rated resources across communities until its
versioned evidence is no longer valid.

`age-minimum` remains a reserved generic wire value but is absent from the
advertised additional-requirements membership catalog, and clients must not
hardcode it. Community content gating consumes the account capability through
specs 010 and 013; it never rewrites the member policy.

Questions to put to Very before any `human.unique` work (owner: evidence/spec
agent; answers recorded in this spec's appendix when received):

1. Can one palm produce multiple Very subject values within one application,
   including the widget and bridge web flows?
2. Can users re-enroll the same palm under another Very account?
3. Does the ZK proof expose a stable palm/person nullifier?
4. What scopes that nullifier: application, external nullifier, purpose,
   verifier?
5. Are liveness, revocation, and duplicate-enrollment handling part of the
   verified result?

These questions may be sent and answered in parallel. They do not block the
v1 `very.web` adapter or the conservative claims frozen above; they block
only a later policy revision that would emit
`human.unique`, claim person-level deduplication, or promise Sybil resistance.

### 2.2 Optional document-nationality requirement

Ratified by workspace_owner on 2026-09-12, amended 2026-09-19. A member policy
is either the Palm policy (`human-verification` alone) or the
document-nationality policy (`nationality-allowed` alone, with no
`human-verification`). A community described as having no nationality gate
keeps the Palm policy; a nationality-restricted community requires one
accepted document proof of nationality and no Palm. Nationality authoring v1 accepts only a nonempty allowlist
of valid, canonical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, distinct and sorted before
hashing. The wizard's `allowedCountries` maps to the verification requirement's
`allowed_countries`. For example, "Nationality: United States" is the
allowlist `["US"]`; the example is illustrative, authoring starts empty and
never preselects a country (2026-09-19 amendment). Exclusion lists are
deferred. Copy describes document nationality,
never residence, location, or a user-declared country.

Self (`self.pass`) and ZKPassport (`zkpassport`) are equal alternatives for
this requirement. The joining user chooses; an author cannot prefer or exclude
one provider. Both adapters must emit `nationality.allowed: { allowed: true }`
only after server verification against the exact normalized requested
allowlist. A boolean detached from that requirement and its persisted proof
session is insufficient. The active Gates v2 compiler and evaluator must be
extended for this predicate; the dormant disclosed-country evaluator is not
an authorization path and must not become a parallel evaluator.

Palm and nationality compose through verified ownership by the same private
account. The two Palm claims retain their same-subject requirement within
Very. No cross-provider subject or nullifier equality is asserted. Document
nationality implies neither `human.personhood`, `credential.subject_unique`,
nor `human.unique`, and an age proof does not satisfy nationality. This
amendment does not change the separate adult-resource or reward policies.

Document-only membership carries weaker assurance than the Palm policy.
Provider-specific duplicate prevention can help within one provider; it does
not resolve the same person joining with different providers or with different
documents, and copy must not describe that gap as solved.

Evidence binds to the exact normalized nationality requirement hash and
server-verified session provenance. Reuse is allowed for the same account and
exact requirement only when the selected receipt's provider binding, scope,
assurance, and freshness satisfy the consuming policy. Never widen an
RP/action scope to obtain reuse. A changed nationality requirement requires
fresh proof in v1; neither subset/superset inference nor a retained country
attribute may satisfy it. A policy revision still requires a new action
decision even if its unchanged nationality requirement can reuse evidence.
Requirement identity, provider binding, and action-policy revision remain
distinct pinned inputs; neither provider choice nor evidence reuse lets the
client replace any of them. Implementation must freeze the successor
canonical preimages and vectors without reinterpreting existing Palm hashes.

Evidence lifetime is an explicit required, versioned policy input. On
2026-09-14 workspace_owner selected one year for both joining and handle
claims: 365 days (31,536,000 seconds) from the accepted evidence observation.
Reuse is refused at that boundary, or earlier when either assertion or receipt
expires or any revocation, account-binding, requirement, scope, assurance, or
provider-binding check fails. Missing or invalid lifetime fails closed and
never means unlimited validity. Freshness uses server evaluation time; replay,
joining, and quoting never renew an observation. Ceremony timeout, quote
expiry, and namespace-authority leases do not define or extend this lifetime.
This decision does not select or change the separate adult-viewing age-evidence
lifetime, enable the feature, or waive compatible-consumer and acceptance gates.
Expiry after a completed join does not introduce continuous membership
re-evaluation in this amendment.

The provider chooser must explain the disclosure difference before launch:
Self discloses the document country to the verifier, which derives the
allowlist predicate; ZKPassport proves the allowlist predicate without
disclosing a separate country attribute. A successful single-country
predicate necessarily reveals that the document matches that country, so the
UI must not promise that the result hides it. Self's transient disclosure must
not reach persisted evidence, logs, or public responses. Retain bounded
provenance and evidence digests, never a reusable country profile. The current
Self adapter already omits the country from receipt metadata; acceptance must
also verify logging, failure paths, and public-response redaction.

## 3. Enforcement model

- Gate evaluation happens at join. Post, comment, and vote writes already
  require active membership (`content-repository.ts` requires it inside the
  write transaction). The account satisfies Palm and any configured
  nationality requirement before joining, with no per-post gate engine.
- Nationality evidence freshness is checked at join under section 2.2.
  Continuous evidence-expiry re-evaluation of existing members remains
  deferred; write enforcement still consumes active membership.
- Gate failures return `GateUnsatisfied` with the missing capability, matching
  the existing join-eligibility contract shape.
- Contract repair accompanies the evaluator slice: the current
  `JoinEligibility` contract (`packages/contracts/src/v1.ts:863`) emits bare
  provider literals (`"very"`, `"self"`) and a `unique_human`-centered
  missing-capability vocabulary. The canonical writer must move it to the
  transport-accurate `very.web` provider id and the
  personhood-plus-subject-unique model, and gain the typed `next_action` field
  specified in spec 010, so claim algebra stays out of UI code. The nationality
  successor updates the contract and generated clients before advertising
  its new requirements.
- For Palm-only policies, the v1 public projection is exact. The gate summary uses
  `gate_type: "human_verification"`, `accepted_providers: ["very.web"]`,
  and missing evidence uses `missing_capabilities: ["human_verification"]`.
  The two internal evaluator claim ids are not separate UI capabilities.
  `next_action` is `start_verification` with `provider_id: "very.web"` when
  evidence is missing, `join` on pass, `blocked` on terminal failure, `wait`
  for an existing pending operation, and `none` for an existing membership.
- A join verification `intent_id` is an opaque server-issued identifier bound
  to the actor, community, current policy identity/hash, requirement hash, and
  persisted provider binding. Clients may only echo it to the generic start
  endpoint. Exact pending/completed starts replay; a failed or expired
  ceremony causes eligibility to issue a fresh generation. Guessing or
  modifying an id cannot select another policy, provider, or actor.
- The nationality successor exposes server-authored missing requirements and
  the two accepted provider choices through a versioned generated contract.
  Persist both complete provider alternatives at policy creation/amendment;
  explicit user selection binds the ceremony session to one of them. Switching
  provider creates a separately bound session, never mutates a pending or
  completed session or silently substitutes a provider. The client echoes
  server-issued authority; it does not compile claim algebra or invent hashes.
- Proof completion persists evidence only. Eligibility is re-fetched and the
  user explicitly joins. That transaction rechecks the current policy and
  evidence and atomically activates membership, its mandatory follow, and
  fulfillment of the applicable join intent. Duplicate completion or join
  replay cannot create another membership, follow, or authorization decision
  for the same idempotent action. A handle-claim intent cannot authorize join.

## 3A. Activity participation and community publication

The owner ratifies this boundary on 2026-09-06. It supersedes any earlier
requirement that an account first join or complete the community's verification
ceremony to Study, sing Karaoke or Dance to available content. Membership is
posting authority, not a proxy for all engagement with a community's content.

| Action | Community posting gate |
| --- | --- |
| Browse or play content | No; existing visibility, age and resource-access rules apply |
| Prepare/select an activity persona, start or resume Study/Karaoke/Dance | No; authenticate, validate ownership and exact community binding |
| Submit answers or private assessment media, receive scores, save progress, complete an attempt | No; enforce consent, integrity, availability and resource limits |
| Study or Karaoke completion | No Post exists or is created; no publish or verification interstitial |
| Publish a Dance recording or another community Post | Yes; ordinary gated membership and publication transaction authority apply |

An unverified or nonmember authenticated account may use the same activity
runtime and receive its ordinary private result. Missing membership, a pending
join or missing Palm/other community proof must not produce membership_required
from an activity command, block a retry/reconnect or be required by the persona
selection screen. A community posting ban does not itself grant authority to
read private content or invent a new activity ban; separate account, persona,
content or resource-access sanctions retain their stated effects.

An account may explicitly select, bind or create an exact-community activity
persona before joining (014 §11.2). This never records membership, satisfies a
gate, follows the community, allocates a wallet or grants a role. Identity
isolation, ownership, immutable binding and account-scoped deduplication remain.
An unbound first persona is prepared explicitly, never silently selected.

Scoring, qualification, private progress and already-admitted nonmonetary
standings are activity effects, not community Posts. They must not depend on
passing the community posting gate. Spec 015's separately specified scarce-leg
eligibility, money admission, solvency and payout controls remain reward-only
checks: an ineligible reward outcome cannot roll back or prevent activity
completion. This amendment neither awards money merely for participation nor
removes those independent financial controls.

Money-admission clarification — ratified by delegated coordinator decision,
2026-09-06. An account with no accepted human-verification evidence may practice,
qualify, keep progress and appear in admitted nonmonetary standings, but cannot
receive a monetary reward: no Megapot beneficiary share, asset-bonus entitlement
or community-token credit. Spec 015 §8 requires the reward's own verified
human.personhood plus credential.subject_unique decision; community membership
is neither necessary nor sufficient. The currently admitted proof is the Very
Palm ceremony. A completed verification does not join a community, and a verified
nonmember may receive an otherwise eligible reward without gaining posting rights.
This preserves a verification barrier to multiple-account reward abuse; it does
not establish human.unique or guarantee one human per account. Section 2's
provider-subject limitation still applies. Standings alone are never money
admission. A missing reward proof is shown only as a reward outcome, not as an
activity-entry requirement or a forced ceremony on activity completion.

The product tells any account without valid Palm evidence, before a rewarded
activity starts, that the activity will not earn monetary rewards without a
palm scan, and offers the scan (Spec 015 §8.1). This includes members admitted
through the document-nationality policy, Palm-policy members whose evidence is
missing or stale, and nonmembers who may run activities without Palm (Spec 019).

Study and Karaoke currently have no publish action. Their learner audio remains
private under Spec 019; completion does not enqueue a video, content Post or
public media registration. Dance assessment media is also private. A user who
chooses to post a Dance recording starts the separate Spec 013 video flow. The
client may preserve a local recording/draft while showing the posting gate, but

## 4. `very.web` provider adapter

Provider id `very.web` represents the two proven browser transports. The
desktop method is `embedded_sdk`; the mobile method is `bridge`, with a
`deeplink` presentation and a `poll` handle. Native OAuth is a separate future
charter and must not be enabled by this work.

Flow:

1. `POST /verification/sessions` creates and persists a provider-bound session.
   Capability detection selects the desktop embedded widget or the mobile
   bridge/deep-link presentation. The presentation payload contains only the
   opaque session and launch data needed by the client.
2. Solid preserves `proof_session_id` while the widget or Very app performs
   the palm ceremony. Mobile web opens `veros://verify` and polls the bridge
   using the server-issued handle; desktop receives the widget result.
3. The authenticated client submits only an opaque `provider_payload_ref` to
   `POST /verification/sessions/:proofSessionId/complete`.
4. The adapter independently fetches the corresponding Very verification and,
   for mobile, bridge session. It checks the persisted session binding,
   provider result, freshness, and terminal state before minting evidence:
   `human.personhood` (`provider_attested`) and
   `credential.subject_unique` from the verified result.

Rules:

- The generic `POST /verification/callbacks/:providerId` endpoint is for
  provider-to-server traffic only and is not part of either browser transport.
- No HTTPS OAuth callback is required. The existing `embedded_sdk`, `deeplink`,
  `poll`, and `none` presentations and the complete endpoint are sufficient.
- Tests use injected Very API, bridge, and widget transports plus the staging
  environment; a staging mock must not create production-shaped evidence.
- No browser fetch proxy, client-declared verification result, local-trust
  completion bypass, or verifier-5xx trust fallback is permitted.

- a persisted provider mode and session, typed

## 0. Scope, precedence, and non-goals

This spec is authoritative for: the account/persona/wallet-assignment
aggregates and their cardinality; which identifiers may appear in public
responses; how content authorship, roles, membership, votes, quotas, and gates
relate to accounts versus personas; per-operation persona and wallet
selection; and the privacy acceptance gates.

It does not change: the Privy authentication contract and session verifier of
spec 003 except where §5 names it; the Very personhood and membership policy of
spec 006 except the account-scoping amendment recorded there; the namespace,
route, and handle-key model of spec 012 except the persona-owner and display
amendments recorded there; or the posting machines of spec 013 except the
authorship-projection amendment recorded there. Where this spec and an earlier
spec disagree on who owns a public identity, this spec controls.

Non-goals for v1: cross-account persona transfer; persona merge or split;
persona-level personhood ceremonies; per-persona membership; more than one
active EVM wallet per persona; per-network EVM address separation; any
non-EVM wallet assignment or integration other than §12's `bitcoin-taproot`
recipient assignment; any production EVM network beyond
Ethereum, the DATA Foundation's DATA Network, and Base 8453; persona-scoped
sessions or tokens; on-chain unlinkability claims of any kind; execution of a
staging or production identity migration without separate authorization.

## 1. Decision

A Pirate **account** is private. It is authenticated by Privy, identified by
the existing canonical `users.user_id`, and is the sole holder of Very
evidence, community membership, voting weight, reward, quota, gate, and
moderation authority. It also holds any historical 16+ attestation and any
verified minimum-age capability from spec 006.

A Pirate **persona** is the public identity. An account owns zero or more
personas, including several personas in the same community. A persona that
participates in community activity is server-bound to exactly one community
for life; only the onboarding or migration-resolution state may be unbound.
Each persona has
its own profile, its own public `persona_id`, its own handle grants, and
its own wallet set. In v1 that set holds at most one active `evm` wallet
assignment, used on Ethereum, DATA Network, and Base 8453, and under §12 at
most one active `bitcoin-taproot` assignment used only to receive native
Spaces names. Public surfaces expose personas only.

Ordinary users, community moderators, search, notifications, feeds, comments,
handle lookups, and profile pages receive no account identifier and no path
that enumerates or correlates sibling personas. Tightly controlled platform
trust-and-safety retains account-level linkage for abuse handling under its
own audited authority.

Your worked example becomes:

```text
Privy DID → private Pirate account (users.user_id)
└── Pokémon membership                       // counted once, account-scoped
    ├── persona_1                             // bound to Pokémon only
    │   ├── handle grant: name.charizard     // HNS family, namespace .charizard
    │   └── wallet set
    │       └── evm → 0xAAA…  (Ethereum, DATA Network, and Base)
    └── persona_2                             // also bound to Pokémon only
        ├── handle grant: name.squirtle      // HNS family, namespace .squirtle
        └── wallet set
            └── evm → 0xBBB…
```

`app.xn--pokmon-dva` remains the community's canonical route. `.charizard` and
`.squirtle` are independently verified handle-sale namespaces associated with
that community; they are not routes and not personas.

## 2. Aggregates, authority, and cardinality

| Aggregate | Authority and visibility | Cardinality |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account | Private; authenticated by Privy; the current canonical `users.user_id` | One Privy account to one Pirate account |
| Membership | Private account-level community admission | At most one per `(community_id, account_id)` |
| Persona | Public identity and profile, privately owned by exactly one account and, once used for community activity, bound to exactly one community | Zero or more per account, including many in one community; at most one community per persona |
| Wallet set / assignment | Private mapping from persona and chain-account kind to provider wallet reference, kind-specific derivation metadata (an HD index for `evm`), and address | One wallet set per persona; v1 permits at most one active `evm` assignment and, under §12, at most one active `bitcoin-taproot` recipient assignment; tombstoned, never recycled |
| Platform-global `.pirate` identity | Public default identity, privately scarce at the account boundary and permanently owned by the initial persona | Exactly one stable identity and one active global label per account in v1 |
| Handle grant | Public structured namespace key (spec 012 §5) owned by a persona | Zero or more per persona; many per account |
| Content authorship | Private `actor_account_id` plus public `author_persona_id` | Every post/comment names exactly one persona |
| Votes, rewards, quotas, gates | Account- or verified-subject-scoped | Personas cannot multiply benefits |
| Roles and moderation | Account holds the authority; a persona presents it | Role summaries expose the presenting persona only |

Invariants:

- A persona belongs to exactly one account for its whole life. Ownership is
  immutable in v1.
- A community-bound persona belongs to exactly one community for its whole
  life. The server owns the association; no request, handle purchase, session,
  presentation row, or client preference may move or reuse it.
- A persona may be `active`, `suspended`, or `retired`. Retirement is
  absorbing; a retired persona's `persona_id`, handles, and wallet assignments
  are never reassigned to another persona.
- Every account has at least one persona after onboarding. The first persona
  is created with the account, initially unbound, and carries the existing
  `.pirate` handle and the existing default embedded wallet as its `evm`
  assignment; this is a storage re-homing of present facts, not a new
  ceremony. The first explicit activity-preparation, membership or community-
  creation commit may bind it once. If it is already bound elsewhere, that commit
  must select a
  persona already bound to the target community or create a new one.
- Membership, voting, rewards, quotas, and gate evaluation read the account.
  Creating a persona never creates membership, never re-runs a personhood
  ceremony, never adds a vote, and never widens a quota.
- A community role (owner, moderator, delegated administrator,
  `manage_routes`, `manage_handle_sales`) is granted to the account. The account designates which of
  its active personas bound to that community presents the role; a
  community's public owner/moderator list shows that persona.

## 3. Persona versus alias

Two product actions are deliberately distinct, and the UI must name them
differently:

- **Add an alias to this persona** attaches another handle grant to the same
  persona only when the grant belongs to the persona's bound community. The
  handles share one profile, one `persona_id`, and the same wallet set. They
  are publicly linked by design. The platform-global `.pirate` grant may
  remain on the first persona, but it is not a community handle and is never
  selected as the display handle on a community-scoped projection.
- **Create a separate persona** creates a new profile, a new `persona_id`, and
  a new wallet set. Nothing public connects it to the account's other
  personas. Cross-community handle acquisition selects this path by default.
  When no persona is already bound to the target community this path is
  mandatory. The new persona begins without an EVM assignment; wallet
  preparation remains lazy until an operation actually needs one.

`name.charizard` and `name.squirtle` require separate personas when their
grants belong to different communities. If both namespaces belong to the same
community, the user may add them to one eligible persona or choose separate
personas there. A handle purchase requires a persona bound to the selling
community, or preparation of an eligible persona there under section 11,
before quoting. It cannot attach the grant to a persona bound elsewhere,
even through an explicit public-linking choice.

Spec 012 §5.1.9 owns the single-use, server-bound confirmation for adding an
alias to an eligible persona with an existing public footprint within the
same community. The server determines whether confirmation is required;
confirmation never bypasses the community-binding requirement.

The server derives the confirmation requirement from the selected persona
and target offering; the client cannot assert that a persona is new or
unlinked. Missing, expired, foreign, stale or mismatched confirmation fails
before quoting or any external effect. The confirmation response and public
projections never reveal sibling personas. Confirmation and alias attachment
do not themselves prepare a wallet; persona provisioning remains governed
by the applicable Spec 014 activation contract.

## 4. Wallet set and v1 EVM assignment

The v1 MVP supports one chain-account kind: `evm`. One persona EVM address is
reused on Ethereum, the DATA Foundation's DATA Network (formerly Story
Network), and Base 8453. Those are separate networks with independent
balances, but they do not require separate wallet assignments. Base Sepolia
84532 is test/staging only. ETH, USDC, `$DATA`, community tokens, and other
currencies are assets held at the address on a network; currencies are not
wallet assignments.

Reusing one EVM address across Ethereum, DATA Network, and Base publicly
correlates a persona with itself across those networks. It does not correlate
that persona with the account's sibling personas, which receive different EVM
addresses. Per-network EVM separation is out of scope unless separately
decided.

- Each persona owns one wallet set. In v1, it holds at most one active `evm`
  assignment, recorded privately as the Privy wallet id, HD wallet index,
  `evm` chain-account kind, and address, and verified against Privy's
  `linkedAccounts` on the authenticated session. The provider wallet id is
  nullable because Privy's user-object contract permits `id: null` for an
  embedded wallet; `(account_id, evm, hd_wallet_index)` and the attested address
  are the assignment authority, never the presence of that provider id.
- The EVM assignment is created lazily on persona creation or first wallet
  need. No other chain-account kind is provisioned in v1 except §12's
  `bitcoin-taproot` recipient assignment, which only its own explicit
  preparation creates.
- Creation requests an explicitly indexed Privy embedded EVM HD wallet. The
  client requests a specific index rather than "create an additional wallet";
  Privy returns the existing wallet when that index already exists, which
  makes assignment replayable and recoverable.
- The server allocates the EVM index. It records the intended `(account_id,
  persona_id, evm, hd_wallet_index)` before the client call and commits the
  address only after it appears in the verified `linkedAccounts`. Index
  allocation is append-only per account.
- An EVM assignment is tombstoned when its persona is retired or when the
  account explicitly re-assigns it. A tombstoned wallet is never assigned to
  a different persona of the same account, and never to another account.
- An account with three wallet-enabled personas therefore holds three distinct
  EVM addresses. Privy's total-wallet, rate-limit, pricing, and recovery
  constraints bound persona cardinality and must be confirmed and recorded in
  Appendix A before any cardinality is promised in product copy. The
  documented "up to 10" figure applies to EVM wallets pregenerated through the
  new-user import endpoint and is not a per-user total.

The wallet-set and `chain_account_kind` vocabulary is retained as a deliberate
extension point, not as a v1 multichain promise. §12 admits exactly one
Bitcoin kind, `bitcoin-taproot`, and only as the recipient key of native
Spaces names; it is not a general Bitcoin wallet. Solana, Bitcoin SegWit,
Cosmos, Tempo, further EVM networks, and other families still require a later
specification amendment that confirms provider support, custody and recovery
behavior, derivation metadata, transaction integration, privacy
consequences, and UI. V1 does not classify Tempo as an EVM network or
separate kind, and does not assume that `hd_wallet_index` applies to every
kind; §12 permits kind-specific derivation metadata for `bitcoin-taproot`
when provider evidence requires it.

Privacy posture that copy must respect: separate addresses do not reveal a
common HD seed by themselves, but that is address-level separation only.
Funding flows, transfers, handle issuance, payments, repeated counterparties,
smart-account ownership, bundler traffic, and behavior can still correlate
them. A shared paymaster avoids funding every persona from one personal wallet
but does not hide the sending EOA or smart-account address and must not be
described as an unlinkability mechanism.

## 5. Session, persona selection, and wallet authority

- The session subject stays account-scoped. Spec 003's session verifier and
  spec 006's evidence binding continue to resolve the account.
- Every operation that acts as or pays from a persona names the persona
  explicitly: `persona_id` in the command, checked server-side to be an active
  persona owned by the session account. Every community-scoped operation also
  names `community_id` and checks the immutable persona binding for that exact
  community plus the account's required membership or capability. A global
  persona list, the first active persona, a handle owned in another community,
  or a previous client selection is never authority or a server fallback.
- Wallet authority is per operation. The server resolves the persona's active
  EVM assignment and requires the client to prove control of that specific
  wallet for that operation. A client-supplied wallet address is never
  sufficient authority, and the login-wide session is never promoted to
  wallet authority. The existing verifier behavior that selects no wallet when
  several exist unless one is explicitly requested is preserved and becomes
  the rule: the requested wallet must equal the persona's assignment.
- Idempotency keys for persona-scoped effects are bound to
  `(account_id, persona_id, endpoint_template, key)`; reuse across personas
  with a different hash is a conflict.

## 6. Public and private projections

Private to the account (owner-scoped endpoints only): the list of its
personas, each persona's wallet set and assignments, each persona's role
designations, the HD index ledger, and membership facts.

Public (feeds, posts, comments, profiles, search, notifications, handle
lookups, role summaries): `persona_id`, the persona's display fields, its
handle grants' display identifiers, and derived public reputation attached to
the persona. No `account_id`, no `user_id`, no wallet id or HD index, no
"also known as" across personas, no "communities created by this account".
Persona-presented song and community streak standings are public under the
same boundary. Megapot pool projections may expose beneficiary counts only,
never beneficiary identities, account aggregates, wallet data, or sibling
links. The viewer's own standing and reward ledger remain private and
`no-store`.

Content authored by a persona remains subject to the viewer-specific rating
guard. A persona page and every handle-host projection preserve the adult
resource's position only through `AgeLockedResourceV1`; they do not expose its
title, body, thumbnail, media URL, comments, or engagement metadata. The
private age capability is resolved for the viewing account and is never added
to a persona response, role summary, or public profile. Internal cache
partitioning may use only the resolved general/adult capability class required
by spec 013, never provider or evidence details.

Concretely:

- `author_user` is replaced by `author_persona` on every public post and
  comment projection; feed projection fills it from `author_persona_id`.
- Public profile resolution follows a handle grant to its persona and stops
  there. It lists only what that persona publicly did. It never resolves to
  the canonical user and never lists communities by creating account.
- Community owner/moderator summaries expose the presenting persona, not a
  `user` identifier.
- A public handle lookup for one handle cannot recover the owner account's
  other handles, personas, or communities.
- Trust-and-safety linkage (account for a given persona, all personas for a
  given account) lives behind the operator authority boundary with audit rows;
  it is never reachable from member or moderator endpoints.

### 6.1 Private aggregated wallet hub — amendment 2026-08-25

The product model is one simple private portfolio over many isolated persona
addresses. Users encounter persona choice when identity or wallet authority
matters, not while casually checking an account balance.

The default hub presents account totals with network and asset sections. It
does not enumerate a persona-by-persona balance ledger or sibling address list;
the selected persona's address and available amount appear only inside an
explicit send, receive, or sign flow.

- The wallet hub is a private, authenticated, account-scoped read model.
- It may aggregate portfolio value and transaction history across every persona
  wallet.
- An aggregate is informational only. It is never a signing balance, spending
  authority, source wallet, or assertion that funds occupy one address.
- Same-symbol assets on different networks remain separately spendable
  balances. For example, USDC on Ethereum and USDC on DATA Network may
  contribute to one displayed portfolio value but cannot be spent as one pool.
- Sending, receiving, and signing always identify exactly one persona and the
  server-resolved wallet assigned to it. A send flow may ask “Pay as Captain /
  Singer / Anon,” then shows only that persona's available amount before
  signing.
- `persona_insufficient_funds` reports only the selected persona's available
  balance. Its payload exposes no sibling persona, address, or balance and the
  product offers no “top up from another persona” action.
- Pirate provides no endpoint or automatic behavior that consolidates,
  balances, sweeps, or transfers value between two persona wallets of one
  account.
- Combined transaction history is owner-private correlation data. It is never
  reused by a public projection and every response carries a private,
  `Cache-Control: private, no-store` policy.
- The on-chain paymaster identity is platform-wide rather than account-scoped.
  Sponsorship calldata contains no stable account-level identifier that could
  correlate sibling personas.
- Account-scoped gas quotas remain private server policy. Neither the shared
  paymaster nor the wallet hub is described as an unlinkability guarantee.

Aggregation is presentation-only because the funds genuinely remain at
different addresses. Presenting one spendable total would create failed sends
and pressure users toward consolidation. Automatic transfers are prohibited
because an on-chain transfer between sibling persona addresses permanently
links them. A per-account sponsor or stable account marker in sponsorship data
would recreate the same linkage through the gas layer. Combined history is the
richest account-level correlation artifact in the product, so its owner-private
and uncacheable boundary is mandatory.

### 6.2 Persona-native public profile — amendment 2026-08-26

The canonical public identity route is
`https://pirate.sc/p/<persona_id_segment>`, where
`<persona_id_segment>` is the exact `encodeURIComponent(persona_id)` result.
The route decodes once to the stored public identifier and performs no case,
Unicode, alias, handle, or account normalization. A persona does not need a
platform-global `.pirate` label to have a canonical profile.

api-next exposes the corresponding unauthenticated endpoint:

```text
GET /public-personas/:personaId
```

Its closed response is:

```ts
type PublicPersonaProfileV1 = {
  persona: PublicPersonaV1;
  profile: {
    revision: number;
    cover_ref: string | null;
    bio: string | null;
  };
  handle_grants: readonly PublicHandleGrantV3[];
};
```

`PublicHandleGrantV3` is the Spec 012 §5.3.10 public grant projection. Every
nested `owner_persona` must byte-for-byte equal the top-level `persona`. The array
contains only active, publicly resolvable grants owned by that persona and is
sorted bytewise by `family`, `namespace_root`, `handle_label`, then
`grant_id`. An unavailable host projection may remain visible for a retained
active grant, but a revoked or tombstoned grant does not. The endpoint returns
the same enumeration-safe `404 not_found` for an unknown, suspended, retired,
or otherwise non-public persona.

The response contains no preferred locale, account or user id, Privy subject,
wallet assignment or address, HD index, membership, account-owned community,
role not presented by this persona, sibling handle, sibling persona, private
reputation evidence, or trust-and-safety linkage. It carries
`Cache-Control: no-store`; no intermediary or browser may reuse a profile
after a persona, grant, or host-authority change. The public Solid
route accepts only `GET` and `HEAD`, uses the same projection, and emits the
persona route above as canonical metadata.

Handle resolution may select this route only after resolving one public grant
to its `owner_persona_id`. It stops at that persona, and the rendered response
must contain the exact active grant and generation that supplied the lookup.
It never falls back to a first persona, a platform-global label, another
handle, or the owning account. Several handles intentionally attached to one
persona therefore share this route; separate personas remain unlinkable by
this surface.

## 10. Wallet-backed public persona activation — ratified 2026-08-26

This amendment supersedes only the lazy-assignment sentences in §§3–4 and the
`at most one` cardinality where an active public persona is concerned. It does
not change the account/persona privacy boundary, wallet authority, public
profile contract, or private wallet-hub presentation.

The invariant is, except for the community-owner publication carve-out in
section 3.1:

- a `pending_wallet` persona is a private provisioning record with exactly one
  reserved account-unique EVM HD index and no confirmed assignment;
- an `active` or `suspended` persona retains exactly one confirmed EVM
  assignment; a freshly published community owner may instead retain exactly
  one reserved pending assignment until ordinary sign-in recovery confirms it;
- retiring a persona tombstones its assignment and its HD index permanently;
- no public persona, profile, handle ownership, authorship, role presentation,
  reward recipient, ordinary persona-switcher item, or public lookup exists
  before activation, except that the atomic community-owner commit activates
  and publishes its named owner profile before wallet confirmation; and
- no availability, quote, reservation, claim, grant, rename, or other handle
  operation prepares or confirms a wallet.

An active persona may have no community handle. Joining a community remains an
account-level membership action and creates no persona or wallet. Conversely,
creating a separate persona while acquiring a handle must finish the persona
provisioning ceremony before the handle quote request begins.
The handle command receives an already-active `persona_id`; it never resumes,
prepares, or confirms the pending persona as a side effect.

### 10.1 Provisioning state machine

The first signup and every later persona use the same two-phase boundary.

1. Inside one database transaction, the server creates the private account if
   needed, creates a `pending_wallet` persona, reserves its next append-only EVM
   HD index, and stores the creation idempotency result. The first persona
   reserves index zero. No public profile or `.pirate` identity is emitted.
2. The authenticated Solid client asks the pinned Privy SDK to create or
   retrieve the explicitly reserved index. It does not ask for an unspecified
   additional wallet.
3. The client submits the returned wallet evidence to the existing confirmation
   boundary. The server verifies the authenticated Privy subject, chain-account
   kind, reserved index, attested address, and nullable provider wallet id
   against current `linkedAccounts`.
4. One transaction locks the pending persona and reservation, records the exact
   assignment, changes the persona to `active`, and creates the public profile.
   For first signup only, it also activates the account's one stable `.pirate`
   identity. Nothing public is committed unless the whole transition succeeds.

The closed lifecycle is:

```text
private pending_wallet -> active -> suspended -> active
                              |           |
                              +-> retired <-+
private pending_wallet -----------------> retired
```

`retired` is absorbing. A pending persona may be retired by an explicit private
cancel action, but the reserved index is tombstoned rather than recycled.
Automatic expiry or deletion of pending personas is not permitted in v1 because
it would make a provider-created address unreachable from Pirate's recovery
ledger.

An exact creation replay returns the same private pending persona and reserved
index. An exact preparation or confirmation retry retrieves or confirms the
same indexed wallet and creates no new slot. Reusing an idempotency key with a
changed request is a conflict. Concurrent creation serializes at the account's
HD-index allocator; concurrent confirmation permits exactly one activation and
returns the stored result to an exact loser replay.

If Privy is unavailable, the private account and pending first persona may
survive. The user receives a retryable setup state and no ordinary authenticated
product session, public profile, global label, role, content authority, handle
quote, or reward surface until confirmation succeeds. Later-persona failure
leaves the existing account and active personas usable while the pending setup
can be resumed privately.

### 10.2 Bounded cardinality

The ratified v1 constants are:

```text
persona_wallet_slot_limit_v1 = 10
persona_wallet_new_slot_limit_v1 = 3
persona_wallet_new_slot_window_v1 = 86400 database-clock seconds
```

Ten is Pirate's product ceiling, not a claim that Privy guarantees ten wallets
per user. Implementation must fail closed below the ceiling if current provider
quota, recovery, or account state cannot safely create the next indexed wallet.

The slot limit counts every HD index ever reserved for the account: private
pending, active, suspended, retired, and tombstoned assignments. The initial
persona consumes one slot. Retiring or cancelling a persona does not restore
capacity because the provider wallet, historical address, and non-recycled
index still exist. Several handles may attach to one persona without consuming
another slot.

The creation rate counts only newly committed additional-persona reservations.
Initial signup is exempt. Exact creation replay, preparation retry, confirmation
retry, activation, suspension, retirement, and attaching another handle to an
existing persona consume no rate event. The server evaluates the rolling window
from its database clock and serializes the count with index reservation, so
concurrent attempts cannot exceed either bound.

At the slot bound, a new reservation fails before any persona id, HD index, or
provider request is created. At the rate bound, it fails retryably with the
database time at which capacity next becomes available, without exposing any
sibling persona, address, or creation timestamp. The owner may raise these
product constants in a later amendment after provider limits and recovery
behavior are confirmed; lowering them may not invalidate retained personas.

### 10.3 Privacy and UI consequences

After activation, the §6.1 select-first rule remains unchanged. Receive, pay,
send, and sign flows first select one persona and only then show that persona's
address or available amount. The wallet hub still does not enumerate sibling
addresses or a persona-by-persona balance ledger. Public responses never expose
an address, HD index, provider id, account-level slot count, or rate state.

## 11. Community binding lifecycle and migration

### 11.1 Binding authority

`persona_community_bindings` is the sole community eligibility authority for
a persona. `binding_source` is a closed value:
`first_membership | community_creation | persona_creation | activity_participation |
migration_single_evidence | explicit_migration_resolution`. Community
retirement or deletion does not release or retarget a binding. A helper
equivalent to
`active_owned_community_persona(account_id, persona_id, community_id)` returns
true only when the persona is active, owned by the account, and has the exact
binding. Membership remains an independent account fact and is checked through
the existing community-effect predicate when the operation requires it. The
two checks are not collapsed into a client claim.

Wallet assignments remain persona-owned. The immutable binding therefore
prevents a community operation from resolving the same persona wallet in a
second community; no community response exposes the address or wallet lineage.

Tables that durably pair a community with a persona use the binding's composite
key wherever a foreign key can express the invariant. Repository commands
recheck the helper for mutable authority, including Study and Karaoke session
start, content authorship, handle acquisition, role and activity presentation,
and exact replays that promise only while authority remains current.

### 11.2 Activity preparation, join, creation, and additional personas

An active membership commit must resolve one of three server-validated cases:

1. select an active owned persona already bound to the target community;
2. bind an active owned unbound persona to that community exactly once; or
3. create a new persona and its target-community binding in the same
   transaction.

The unbound case is serialized on the persona so concurrent joins to different
communities cannot both win. A changed target returns a typed conflict and
does not leave an active membership without an eligible persona. A gated join
resolves the persona only at the terminal membership commit; an intent does not
pre-bind identity.

Community creation applies the same rule atomically with the creator
membership and role presentation. A `create_new` choice lets the server mint
the persona and bind it to the newly allocated community in that commit. A
browser does not invent the binding or a persona id. Creating further personas
requires authenticated ownership, an active target community and the ordinary
account quota/abuse controls; it does not require posting membership or a proof.
The new persona is born bound there. Several personas may share that community,
but none may share another.

Explicit activity preparation uses the same three identity choices above before
any join: select an existing target-bound persona, bind an owned unbound persona
once, or create a bound persona. The server validates target access and identity,
serializes the one-time binding and records activity_participation as its source.
It atomically establishes an absent activity presentation using the selected
persona, preserving an existing explicit presentation. It creates no membership,
follow, role or wallet and invokes no verification provider. A later join can
reuse this binding and presentation after its own gates pass. An activity command
still names the prepared persona explicitly; it never chooses a global default.

Following, previewing, or signing in on a community origin creates no persona.
Explicit activity preparation, joining or creating may create one because an
activity needs an eligible community persona, not because it needs membership.

### 11.3 Retirement and retained history

Retirement never removes or changes the binding. Historical posts, comments,
attempts, qualifications, payout evidence, and immutable presentation history
retain their original persona id and community. A retired persona cannot
author, perform, acquire a handle, start a session, or become a new current
presentation.

If a persona is the current role or activity presentation, ordinary retirement
must atomically designate another active persona bound to the same community.
When none exists and a current presentation is still required, retirement is
rejected until the account creates one. Account erasure remains governed by
spec 023 and may replace retained display data with its generic retired
pseudonym without changing persona ids, bindings, or immutable history.

### 11.4 Contextual public handles

Community-scoped projections select handles only from active grants issued by
that community's handle authority and owned by the projected bound persona.
They do not fall back to an active grant from another community or to the
platform-global `.pirate` grant. No handle is a valid result. Global
`/p/<persona_id>` and exact `.pirate` resolution may still expose the global
grant, but cannot enumerate the owning account or another persona.

### 11.5 Backfill and conflict handling

Before installing binding-enforced foreign keys, a read-only preflight derives
the set of community ids evidenced for every persona from authorship, community
handle grants, role and activity presentations, Study and Karaoke sessions and
attempts, and qualifications. The migration then follows these rules:

- exactly one evidenced community creates one immutable binding;
- no evidenced community leaves the persona unbound and ineligible until an
  explicit account choice binds it; this is the normal first-platform-persona
  state when the account has never participated in a community;
- more than one evidenced community aborts the migration before any schema or
  data commit, emits only bounded conflict identifiers to operator evidence,
  and requires explicit resolution. It never chooses the earliest, latest,
  most-used, handle-owning, or leaderboard community and never rewrites public
  history to make a guess fit.

The preflight and migration use the same versioned evidence query and digest.
No permissive compatibility fallback is allowed after the new predicate is
enabled. A separately authorized staging or production run must record the
zero-, one-, and multi-community counts, the conflict disposition, migration
checksum, and rollback rehearsal without exposing account-to-persona linkage.

### 11.6 Binding acceptance

- Schema tests reject a second community for one persona and reject every
  community/persona child row without the exact composite binding.
- Join and creation races prove one target wins and no active membership or
  role presentation is orphaned.
- Nonmember activity preparation replays exactly, creates only the selected
  binding and absent activity presentation, and leaves membership, follow, role
  and wallet tables untouched. Concurrent preparation/join cannot rebind a
  persona or overwrite an existing activity presentation.
- Persona selection and preparation are available without Palm or another
  community proof; activity commands still reject an unprepared persona.
- A first unbound platform persona binds once; a later community requires an
  existing target-bound or new persona. Same-community additional personas

## 12. Persona Taproot recipient for native Spaces names — ratified 2026-09-23

This amendment supersedes five earlier statements:

1. the §0 non-goal excluding every non-EVM wallet assignment;
2. the §4 sentence that no other chain-account kind is provisioned;
3. the §4 deferral of Bitcoin and the Taproot choice;
4. the §7 rule that storage validates only `evm`;
5. Appendix A's classification of `bitcoin-taproot` as future evidence only.

It changes nothing about the EVM assignment, the §10 activation invariant, the
§10.2 slot and rate constants, per-operation wallet authority in §5, or the
private wallet hub of §6.1.

### 12.1 Assignment, purpose, and cardinality

A persona's wallet set may hold at most one active `bitcoin-taproot`
assignment. Its only purpose is to be the recipient key of native Spaces names
issued under Spec 012 §5.3.13. It is not a general Bitcoin wallet. This
amendment adds no balance display, receive-address projection, send, fee
payment, arbitrary signing surface, or wallet-hub network section for it.
Solana, Cosmos, Tempo, Bitcoin SegWit, further EVM networks, and every other
family still require their own amendment.

The assignment is lazy. It is created only by an explicit Taproot preparation
action, and only when a persona first needs a Spaces recipient. Persona
creation, activation, joining, activity preparation, community creation, and
HNS handle flows never create it. A persona without one is fully active under
§10. Spec 012 availability, quote, reservation, claim, grant, rename, and host
projection never prepare or confirm it; quote, reservation, and claim only read
an assignment that is already confirmed (Spec 012 §5.3.13.6).

The assignment is bound to one Bitcoin network. Production uses only `mainnet`.
Any test network is used only in an isolated environment whose database never
holds production assignments.

Two personas never share a Taproot key or output script, including two personas
of the same account. A Taproot assignment is tombstoned when its persona
retires or its account is erased. It is never recycled and never reassigned to
another persona or account.

Because an account has at most one Taproot assignment per persona, its Taproot
assignments can never outnumber its persona slots. A Taproot assignment
therefore consumes no §10.2 persona-wallet slot and no creation-rate event.
Implementation must still fail closed if the provider's current quota, rate
limits, or account state cannot safely create the assignment.

### 12.2 Provisioning, recovery, and stored facts

Provisioning goes through the existing provider and the existing account
authorization path. The server persists a provisioning intent, naming the
account, persona, kind, and network, before any external create. Recovery is
idempotent for this kind. An exact retry returns the same assignment and
creates nothing new, and reusing an idempotency key with a changed request is a
conflict. Concurrent preparation for one persona permits exactly one confirmed
assignment.

Before implementation, the implementing task confirms the provider's actual
contract for `bitcoin-taproot` and records it in Appendix A. That contract
covers creation, retrieval after a lost response, attestation of ownership on
the authenticated session, and export or recovery. Nothing about the EVM
contract is assumed to carry over. In particular, neither the indexed HD
creation recipe nor the `linkedAccounts` attestation shape is assumed to apply
to Bitcoin. For this kind, `hd_wallet_index` may be null or replaced by
kind-specific derivation metadata where the provider evidence requires it. The
`(account_id, chain_account_kind, hd_wallet_index)` ledger uniqueness applies
only where an index exists.

Confirmation derives the account and provider evidence from the authenticated
session, never from client-supplied ownership. It verifies the provider
subject, kind, network, and address. The P2TR output script is derived by a
standard implementation from the verified address, or from a verified internal
key by applying the BIP-341 tweak. The provider's compressed public key is an
internal key, not the output key, and is never placed in a script directly.

The stored facts are private: the provider wallet reference, network, verified
address, exact output-script bytes, kind-specific derivation and attestation
metadata, status, and times. The recipient script used for issuance is exactly
the stored script.

If the provider fails, the persona stays active and fully usable. A Spaces
quote is refused with Spec 012's `recipient_wallet_required`, and the member
receives a retryable private setup state.

### 12.3 Buyer control and the interoperability gate

Consumer Spaces claims stay disabled until a bounded interoperability exercise
passes. The exercise runs in the account's actual provider execution mode and
establishes each of the following:

1. The provider can create one distinct Taproot wallet per persona for the same
   user, with an association that survives retry and recovery. If the provider
   supports only one such wallet per user, the path fails this gate, because
   sibling personas would share a publicly visible key.
2. The derived output script equals the script decoded from the provider's
   verified address.
3. A key-path signature on a transaction input that spends that exact script
   verifies independently.
4. The holder can produce the ownership signature that the pinned Spaces
   verifier accepts for a handle bound to that script.
5. Recovery or export works for this wallet kind.
6. Two aliases of one persona, bound to the same script, both verify through
   the accepted Spaces verifier and relay.

The exercise records the execution mode, the signature scheme, and each
independently verified result. It distinguishes fixture checks from live
verification. The live alias check may be completed in the first controlled
issuance cohort of Spec 012 §5.3.13.13.

Documented provider capabilities are not evidence that the selected account and
execution mode pass. If the exercise fails, the Taproot path stays disabled and
the recipient decision returns to `workspace_owner`. There is never a fallback
to an operator-held key, a buyer-supplied key, a shared key, or a general
wallet. Buyer-supplied keys, custom script trees, and automatic native key
rotation are outside this amendment.

Verified provider ownership removes the need for a redundant recipient
signature at claim time. It never replaces account authentication, persona
authority, or claim authorization.

### 12.4 Privacy and permanence

A native name binds `label@root` to the persona's Taproot output key publicly
and permanently on the Spaces network, because Spaces certificates are public.
Aliases of one persona share that key and are therefore linkable at the
protocol level, which matches the public linkage §3 already gives aliases.
Separate personas have separate keys and are not linked by them.

Pirate's public projections never add the Taproot address, script, provider
reference, or assignment identifier. The owning account may see its selected
persona's script in owner-only Spaces claim responses, following the
select-first rule of §§6.1 and 10.3. The operator and prover receive only the
name and the script, or hashes of them. They never receive the account,
persona, or any sibling fact.

The Spaces network may show a staged name before Pirate shows it, because the
upstream operator publishes temporary certificates for staged names. Product
copy must not describe a pending name as secret.

Retiring a persona, or erasing its account under Spec 023, tombstones the
Taproot assignment and Pirate's grant. It cannot remove a finalized native name
from the Spaces protocol, and Pirate cannot revoke or erase that name. The
first Spaces claim discloses this permanence before quoting. Spec 023's erasure
copy must say the same before native names are enabled; that alignment is a
follow-up and is not decided here.

### 12.5 Storage and acceptance

`persona_wallet_assignments` admits `chain_account_kind = 'bitcoin-taproot'`
beside `'evm'`. Kind-specific checks cover the address format, the network, and
the exact script bytes. The existing single-live-row index on `(persona_id,
chain_account_kind)` provides the one-per-persona rule. Addresses and scripts
are unique across the table. For this kind, the index column is nullable where
provider evidence requires it. The EVM checks are not loosened.

Acceptance fixtures must prove each of the following:

- A persona holds at most one live Taproot assignment, and two personas of one
  account never share a Taproot key or script.
- Persona creation, activation, joining, activity preparation, community
  creation, and every handle command create no Taproot assignment.
- Preparation replay, changed-request conflict, concurrent preparation, and
  provider failure each have one deterministic result that leaves the persona
  usable.
- The stored script equals an independent BIP-341 derivation from the verified
  address or internal key.
- Tombstoning never recycles or reassigns an assignment.
- No public response contains the Taproot address, script, provider reference,
  or assignment identifier.
- A Spaces quote for a persona without a confirmed assignment fails with
  `recipient_wallet_required` before any write.
- The §10 invariants, slot and rate counting, and EVM fixtures pass unchanged.

This amendment authorizes specification and local implementation and tests. It
creates no wallet, calls no provider, signs nothing, and changes no live
account.

## 3. Bootstrap, delayed responses and recovery

The supported rewarded browser profile requires HTTPS, host-only cookies, same-origin Web Locks and an IndexedDB transaction for a nonsecret selection pointer. Solid takes `navigator.locks.request("pirate.guest-authority.v1", {mode:"exclusive"}, ...)` around bootstrap, confirmation, selection persistence, rotation and the first lesson start. The lock is an application coordination primitive, not authentication. A client assertion that it has a lock supplies no server authority. Unknown browsers and deliberate cookie omission remain part of the abuse review.

`guestAuthoritySelection` in IndexedDB contains only `{origin, owner_id, credential_id, last_start_key}`. It cannot authenticate a request and must never contain a secret or token. It prevents a late empty bootstrap response from becoming the selected identity. Other tabs acquire the same lock and reread the pointer and server authority; a BroadcastChannel notification may update their UI but cannot authorize anything.

The exact sequence after a deliberate Start is:

1. Under the lock, call `GET /guest/authority` with cookies. If the stored selection has valid proof, use it. If its proof is absent or revoked, return `recovery_required`; do not silently overwrite the selection or imply its chance transferred. If there is no selection and exactly one confirmed owner is proved, select it. If multiple established owners are proved, return `authority_conflict`; never merge their lessons or rewards.
2. With no established owner, `POST /guest/bootstrap` issues one pending owner/credential and its uniquely named cookie. The request is JSON with exact Origin and guest CSRF; the prior safe authority read may issue only CSRF, without creating an owner. The response contains nonsecret credential metadata. Existing valid selected proof makes this operation return that authority without issuing another cookie.
3. `POST /guest/bootstrap/confirm` must receive the pending credential cookie on a subsequent request. It locks that credential and owner, checks Origin/CSRF, transitions it to confirmed and starts the one-hour lease. Confirmation records receipt of ownership proof, not a lesson or reward. Same-proof replay returns the same owner. A lost initial Set-Cookie leaves an empty pending owner only.
4. Commit the nonsecret confirmed selection to IndexedDB before posting any lesson start. `POST` start names `expected_owner_id` and the immutable `idempotency_key`; the server derives ownership from the cookie and rejects mismatch. Hold the Web Lock through the start response or an authenticated lookup of an uncertain outcome. After a crashed tab, the next tab recovers by the stored selection and the same start key.

Distinct cookie names ensure a delayed response cannot overwrite a credential used by a lesson. The selected credential remains authoritative even if an older pending cookie arrives afterward. Under the browser lock, authenticated cleanup revokes and expires unselected empty candidates. It must not revoke a credential that has a session or money. At most four guest credential cookies are accepted by this protocol: selected, pending successor, and two abandoned candidates. With additional cookies, return `credential_cleanup_required` without starting rewarded work; a bounded recovery endpoint enumerates only correctly proved credential metadata and expires empty candidates. The cleanup endpoint is callable when the normal four-cookie admission cap is exceeded; it has a separate hard cap of sixteen parsed credential cookies within the existing total header byte bound, validates each presented proof, and can only expire valid empty candidates. This is one bounded pass, not recursive bootstrap or owner selection. Beyond that recovery cap, return a clear manual cookie-cleanup refusal without creating or replacing authority. Oversized headers fail closed under the transport's existing byte bound.

Server confirmation must refuse automatic selection when another established owner is co-present. When all co-present owners are empty, deterministically retain the earliest `(created_at, owner_id)` under row locks and record immutable empty-bootstrap aliases; all such credentials resolve to that one owner. Alias creation is forbidden after a session exists. An authenticated alias result may update the selection pointer only when the response proves that predecessor had no session; otherwise an owner mismatch is a conflict. No database routine claims to identify the same browser if the requests present disjoint proofs. Web Lock serialization and selection persistence establish the supported application's guarantee; the acceptance fixtures must include the delayed-cookie and tab-crash schedules explicitly.

Without Web Locks or durable selection storage, the website still offers an explicitly disclosed practice-only lesson through bounded guest authority, with no chance claimed for that session. It must not show a registration wall or label that lesson rewarded. Closing this browser support gap, if required by staging device acceptance, requires a reviewed coordination alternative before expanding rewarded support; do not silently substitute a client-generated bearer or fingerprint.

Credential rotation uses the same lock and distinct cookie names. Valid current proof creates one pending successor for the same owner; the old credential remains valid until a subsequent request proves receipt of the successor and acknowledges it. Acknowledgement atomically confirms the successor and revokes its predecessor. Lost issuance can be retried with the old proof; lost acknowledgement is resolved using the successor cookie. A delayed revoked cookie never revives server authority. If acknowledgement committed but the IndexedDB update did not, the authority read must accept the proved confirmed successor of the selected credential, verify their common immutable owner, and return pointer-repair metadata under the browser lock. A revoked predecessor pointer alone cannot force a new owner or block a valid proved successor. Pending successor lifetime is fifteen minutes; automatic rotation is not required for this first release. Explicit compromise revocation invalidates credentials and preserves all records and liabilities.

After complete proof loss, the server never uses owner IDs, email hints, IP addresses, browser fingerprints or chat history to restore authority. A deliberate fresh-start action may create separate future learning authority with clear loss-of-access copy; it does not recover an old chance. An already attached owner is recovered by ordinary account login on any admitted product origin.

Use PostgreSQL transaction-scoped advisory locks. Reserve `(83000003, 1)` as the participation-identity barrier after checking the owning source registry for collisions. Admission, claim preparation and owner-aware learning mutation take it shared; bootstrap aliasing and account association take it exclusive. This small global barrier serializes identity topology changes, not provider calls or whole lessons. Existing account media locks remain respected; guest owner locks use a distinct registered namespace.
