Freeze takes drawing then funding locks and never acquires the identity barrier or owner locks afterward: it reads committed immutable shares, so it cannot form a cycle with attachment. No external call occurs while holding these locks.

Provider transcription/scoring executes under the existing durable command reservation outside the final transaction. Finalization verifies the authoritative provider result, commits the server's qualification decision and attempts admission in one short transaction. Learning success plus an ordinary reward refusal is a valid committed result. `entry_closed`, ineligible, duplicate, held or unfunded conditions must not raise a trigger exception that rolls back an otherwise valid lesson completion.

The admission linearization point is the guarded share insert's database `clock_timestamp()`, sampled after locks and immediately before insertion; persist it as `admitted_at`. It must be strictly less than cutoff, with a v3 drawing still `entry_open` and a valid qualification/eligibility decision at that point. It is not lock acquisition, request arrival or a client time. A transaction whose guarded insert occurs before cutoff is admitted if that transaction commits, including a commit completed after cutoff or after the execution deadline. A rollback never admitted anything. A deadline or disconnected caller cannot reclassify an eventual committed insert as absent, late or forfeited.

The implementation must apply PostgreSQL 17 transaction_timeout of three seconds, lock_timeout of 250 ms, statement_timeout of two seconds and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout of two seconds on the dedicated finalization transaction. Set and verify the transaction-local configuration. These settings constrain cancellable transaction work and idle abandonment; they do not establish a hard wall-clock commit bound. PostgreSQL disables transaction_timeout before recording commit and can defer interruption during commit. Issue no provider/network calls inside the transaction and prohibit PREPARE TRANSACTION, prepared transactions and two-phase commit on this path. Reuse the existing Postgres adapter outcomeCertainty classification for sent-COMMIT uncertainty. The owner-admission integration must distinguish failure before COMMIT, acknowledged COMMIT and a sent COMMIT with unknown outcome, cancel cancellable work, and reconcile the last case by immutable operation identity. A client-side timer alone is insufficient. Acceptance must exercise server-enforced cancellation and transport loss during COMMIT, including acknowledgment delayed beyond three seconds and delayed durable commit or equivalent controlled uncertainty. The oracle is authoritative final database state and exact original-drawing inclusion, never a requirement to cancel an irreversible commit. Unsupported timeout configuration or missing uncertainty recovery fails readiness and keeps v3 disabled.

Freeze starts at cutoff and acquires the drawing lock after preceding admissions commit or abort. It counts only committed shares and makes its snapshot/state transition atomically. It cannot omit a lock-holding admission to meet a purchase deadline. Failure to resolve admission or commit within the execution budget stops freeze/purchase progression and records an operational hold outside the unresolved transaction. Do not issue a purchase while drawing-lock acquisition, the admission transaction or its commit outcome is unresolved. Reconciliation must establish authoritative commit/rollback and include every committed pre-cutoff guarded insert before freeze can proceed. An external observation cannot override an unresolved drawing lock, and hold expiry cannot discard a participation. The hold can remain beyond three seconds; there is no promised maximum commit or reconciliation duration. No purchase occurs from a potentially incomplete beneficiary set. Existing purchase safety margins and stale-observation refusal remain stronger constraints. A final grade arriving after cutoff records learning completion and `entry_closed`; it never backdates or targets the next drawing.

Lost responses use the existing immutable operation key plus authenticated owner lookup. An outcome-unknown transaction is reconciled before another command is accepted for that operation. If it did not commit, a later retry re-evaluates current time; an earlier failed attempt is not entitlement. The UI reports pending confirmation until the server knows whether admission committed. Freeze must read beneficiaries in a new READ COMMITTED statement after acquiring the drawing lock, as the existing cutoff reader does, or use an independently proved equivalent fresh-snapshot protocol. Do not take the beneficiary snapshot before waiting for admission to release that lock. Reward lock contention must preserve the durable grading result: use a reviewed savepoint/refusal boundary or command finalization retry that does not regrade or repay the provider; never catch a PostgreSQL transaction-abort error and pretend the lesson committed.

## 10. Signup, association and conflicts

Signup begins on the original product origin. `guest_attachment_intents` records opaque ID, guest owner and credential, origin, nonce digest, state, creation and fifteen-minute expiry. The nonce is a 32-byte random ceremony value held in an HttpOnly host-only cookie, never in a redirect URL; the intent ID is not authority. Only one live intent per guest owner is allowed. Expiry ends that ceremony, not the owner or chance; valid guest proof can create a new intent.

Reuse ordinary provider authentication and `registerIdentity`/credential uniqueness. Do not create a special registration identity from a guest ID, and do not trust a bot, email hint or signup callback as guest proof. The provider return stays on the initiating origin. After authentication, show the explicit account to which the existing history will attach, then confirm through the same-origin API with both proofs, CSRF, nonce and a digest of the current account session, as existing Telegram browser transactions do. A changed session/account before confirmation requires a new protected confirmation, not inferred authority.

Under the exclusive identity barrier, lock the owner, account, intent and all relevant associations in stable order. Recheck account status, guest proof, nonce, intent target and every admitted participation across its original owner and target account's group. A fresh account with no overlap binds the existing owner once. Existing-account attachment succeeds only when its participation scopes are disjoint. Neither outcome changes prior shares, snapshots, allocations or credit identities.

If a scope overlaps, commit `participation_conflict` with its minimal private overlap references and the immutable target account association; preserve all guest rights and proof. Return an explicit conflict, not attachment success. Future qualification on either associated side deduplicates against that group, including races that were waiting on the barrier. Normal code cannot delete that fact, bind to a different account, merge money or create another account to bypass it. No automatic conflict-resolution action is provided in this release; the held rights remain recoverable through their original proof, and any exceptional resolution needs a separately reviewed procedure.

Successful attachment consumes the intent and revokes guest credentials. The authenticated account becomes the access authority from any supported browser/origin. In-flight accepted provider commands may finalize against their immutable source owner under the shared deduplication barrier; browser retries use account authority. If the confirmation response is lost, account-only attachment lookup returns the same binding. If registration succeeded but attachment did not, ordinary provider replay resolves the same account and surviving guest proof resumes the ceremony. Wallet setup failure cannot erase or duplicate that account or pending chance.

Before commit, cancellation changes no ownership; guest learning can continue. Account switching must be visible and re-confirmed before any target is pinned. After a successful or conflict association, normal target reassignment is refused. Attachment does not join a community, issue a name, select a public persona, re-run a lesson, backfill Telegram practice, qualify other reward classes or consume Very.
